planning_output.case_id: ID of the paper or case. Example: Bruner_ExpEco_2017_amYY.
planning_output.planned_id: Unique ID for this planned path. Example: Bruner_ExpEco_2017_amYY_path04.
planning_output.path_summary: Short summary of the proposed analysis path.

path_signature.main_predictor: Main predictor, treatment, or grouping variable.
controls: List of control variables, or empty list.
path_signature.sample_restriction: Sample inclusion or exclusion rule, or null.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Missing data handling rule, or null.
path_signature.variable_construction: How the main variables are created or changed before analysis, or null.
path_signature.inference_rule: How the result will be judged.

planning_output.hypothesis: Focal hypothesis for the claim, phrased as a testable statement.

data_plan.source_type: Data source, such as survey, experiment, database, or archive.
data_plan.wave_or_subset: Specific waves, subsets, or sample restrictions, if applicable.
data_plan.sample_size: Expected sample size if known, otherwise not_stated.
data_plan.unit_of_analysis: Unit of analysis, such as individual, household, country, firm, or trial.
data_plan.access_details: Local path, repository link, access restriction, or not_stated.

steps: Ordered step 1 for preparing and analyzing the data.
Ordered step 2 for preparing and analyzing the data.

tasks.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.
Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

models.type: Model or statistical approach. Example: linear regression, logistic regression, t-test, correlation.
models.planned_estimation: Main quantity to estimate. Example: coefficient, mean difference, odds ratio, correlation.
models.inference_criteria: Rule for judging the result. Example: expected direction and p < 0.05.
models.deviation: true if this uses a meaningful different choice from the original paper, otherwise false.
models.qualification: Explain why this model is a valid way to test the focal claim.

variables.type: Dependent, Independent, Control, Grouping, or Weight.
variables.name: Variable name or constructed variable name.
variables.description: What the variable means and how it is used.
variables.variable_construction: How this variable is created, recoded, scaled, transformed, or aggregated. Use null if the raw variable is used.
variables.missing_data_handling: Rule for missing data, such as listwise deletion or imputation.
variables.deviation: true if this uses a meaningful different choice from the original paper, otherwise false.
variables.qualification: Explain why this variable choice is valid for the focal claim.
models: List of model_id values that use this variable.

planned_method.tools_software: Software or tools expected for execution, such as R, Python, Stata, or specific packages.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Explain how the path tests the same focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Explain how the path uses the original dataset, or null if not applicable.
method_justification.method_reason: Explain why the model, variables, and inference rule are reasonable.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Explain why this path is different from paths already in shared memory.

files.file_name: Short description of each original source code file relevant to this plan. Use null if no code is available.

codebase.notes: Notes about code availability, unclear entry files, dependencies, or folder structure.

self_check.closest_memory_path_id: Path ID of closest existing path, or null.
self_check.self_check_note: Short explanation of the self check.
